usageNotes: Use this to provision a new Ceph OSD on a bare block device attached to the target node; the node must be online and already joined to the Ceph cluster before calling this. The operation is asynchronous — the return value is a task UPID; poll the task status endpoint to confirm the OSD comes up. The target device will be wiped, so ensure it holds no data and is not mounted.

examples.summary: Create a basic OSD on /dev/sdb with a separate NVMe DB device

tips: Use 'osds-per-device' (≥2) only on high-throughput NVMe drives; it is mutually exclusive with db_dev and wal_dev.
Set 'encrypted' to true before the OSD is created — encryption cannot be toggled after the fact.
crush-device-class should match the physical media type ('hdd', 'ssd', or 'nvme') so CRUSH rules can tier storage correctly.
db_dev and wal_dev should reside on a faster device (SSD/NVMe) than the main OSD device to improve small-write performance.
